title: Haiku 5.5 is measured against the current model on the census's agentic steps, the phase-2 reader groups and the kb-census orchestrator, and takes each where it loses nothing that matters
goal: Two agentic census steps are run on claude-haiku-5-5 and on their current model with pinned full names [DOC S-ezqg74ki], from the same brief, caps and permission rules: (1) census.py dispatch on held-out phase-2 groups whose outcomes the census already recorded, each result checked by census.py apply --dry-run (schema-valid, ids known, files owned) and compared per source with the recorded outcome (confirmed, updated, superseded, gone), a false confirm (confirmed where the census changed a fact) counting as the critical error; (2) the kb-census skill's orchestrator on a census of one small selection after sprints 1 and 2, compared on whether it ran the commands in the skill's order, stopped where the skill says, applied every group and reported the counts the skill's Report section asks for. Haiku becomes the step's default (dispatch's --model default; the model the kb-census skill names for its orchestrator, if the skill can name one) only when it has no more false confirms or skipped steps than the current model, its outcome agreement is within 5 points, and its turns stay under the cap; otherwise the step keeps its model and the result names the failing bar. Each run is a --dry-run estimate first with --max-budget-usd from it; per step and model, agreement, critical errors, turns, tokens, USD from total_cost_usd and wall time are recorded in kb/_self/reports/fact-diff.md beside the single-call steps' section, with the commands that produced them.

gates.question: What does a dispatch run's --max-budget-usd come from in the comparison?
options: 3 times the dry run's estimate (factdiff.call_cap), at least 0.25 USD; a capped group rerun once at 1.00 USD, as the skill's rule says
the default census.DISPATCH_BUDGET_USD (5.00) for every run
gates.recommendation: 3 times the dry run's estimate (factdiff.call_cap), at least 0.25 USD; a capped group rerun once at 1.00 USD, as the skill's rule says

gates.question: Under which caps and permission rules does each model run the kb-census orchestrator in the comparison?
options: 150 turns and 5.76 USD (3 times the list-price estimate of an Opus 5.5 session of about 70 turns), dontAsk with python3 _tools/*, git add/commit/status/diff/log/show/tag, Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Agent and Skill allowed, the same for both models
the 60 and 5.00 USD of a dispatched worker, the same allow list
gates.recommendation: 150 turns and 5.76 USD (3 times the list-price estimate of an Opus 5.5 session of about 70 turns), dontAsk with python3 _tools/*, git add/commit/status/diff/log/show/tag, Read, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Agent and Skill allowed, the same for both models

gates.question: Which sources does the dispatch comparison score, and what is a false confirm and a skipped group?
options: the held-out half's rows with a recorded outcome other than unconfirmed and no techcommunity host (114 sources, 18 groups); a false confirm is confirmed where the census recorded updated, superseded or gone; a result apply --dry-run refuses or a run that returned none counts as unconfirmed and as a skipped group
only rows the census recorded updated or confirmed; a false confirm is confirmed against updated alone
gates.recommendation: the held-out half's rows with a recorded outcome other than unconfirmed and no techcommunity host (114 sources, 18 groups); a false confirm is confirmed where the census recorded updated, superseded or gone; a result apply --dry-run refuses or a run that returned none counts as unconfirmed and as a skipped group

gates.question: What do the estimate constants of census.py dispatch --dry-run and the command that scores results against a census log look like?
options: census.DISPATCH_BASE_TOKENS 15000, DISPATCH_PAGE_CHARS 26000, DISPATCH_TURNS_PER_ROW 4, DISPATCH_REPLY_TOKENS 800, the cap 3 times the USD (factdiff.call_cap); a read-only census.py score LOG --from RESULTS.json ... command
no estimate in dispatch --dry-run and the scoring kept out of the repository
gates.recommendation: census.DISPATCH_BASE_TOKENS 15000, DISPATCH_PAGE_CHARS 26000, DISPATCH_TURNS_PER_ROW 4, DISPATCH_REPLY_TOKENS 800, the cap 3 times the USD (factdiff.call_cap); a read-only census.py score LOG --from RESULTS.json ... command

notes: Same pricing, pinning and effort facts as ST-jkehwsu4 (public/claude/ci-and-headless.md:83-89). The agentic comparison costs more than the single-call one, so it runs after ST-jkehwsu4 and on few groups: the count is set from the dry-run estimate, and the groups are drawn from the held-out half ST-jkehwsu4 split. A smaller orchestrator matters only once sprints 1 and 2 have moved most of its work into census.py commands; before that its turns are mostly reading and editing, the work this comparison would penalise Haiku for. AGENTS.md is reviewed, not edited (its 4 KB cap). The 5-point bar is the session's proposal, open to change at the start gate. 2026-10-11 orchestrator (operator's delegate, unattended run): paid comparison runs are approved within the goal's dry-run-then-cap rule; the item's whole spend stays under 25 USD (a ceiling set without data: when the estimate for the planned set exceeds it, shrink the set and say so in the report, or stop on a gate). The orchestrator comparison (2) runs on a throwaway clone under the scratch directory: no kb content it writes is committed, only the measurements and the commands. ST-jlezjp6k landed census.py dispatch with DISPATCH_MODEL claude-sonnet-5-5 and caps 150 turns, 5.00 USD per part (its gates g1, g3).
